137	pub struct SealBinding { /* read-only accessors for the 13 association values */ }
138	pub enum EvidenceCommitOutcome { Committed, Undetermined }
139	pub trait SealedEvidenceCommit {
140	    /// Called at most once, under the held append lock, after the SEAL record

143	        -> Result<EvidenceCommitOutcome, EvidenceCommitError>;
144	}
145

147	pub struct JournalWriteTxn<'s>(/* private */);        // !Clone !Copy !Default, no Serialize,
148	                                                      // no public write method, lifetime-bound to the session
149	impl<'s> JournalWriteTxn<'s> { pub fn abort(self); }  // the ONLY other public operation
150	impl<'s> Drop for JournalWriteTxn<'s> { /* rollback; fail-stop on leak */ }

153	pub fn seal_under_append_lock(
154	    txn: JournalWriteTxn<'_>,            // consumed
155	    session: CommitSession,              // consumed  -> no further effect from this session

158	) -> SealOutcome;                        // Committed | Undetermined | Refused{cause, sealDurable}

161	Why this satisfies every constraint you set:
162	
163	- **Private SQL and session authority stay inaccessible.** The guard has no write method; the session is moved, not borrowed.
164	- **Security does not depend on storage.** The callback trait lives in `contracts`; security takes `&mut dyn SealedEvidenceCommit`.
165	- **Both transactions precede the append lock.** Storage: `begin_journal_txn` (L3) → open its own evidence transaction (L3) → `seal_under_append_lock` (takes L4 internally). If the evidence acquisition fails, storage calls `txn.abort()` — which is why `abort` must exist.
166	- **The callback cannot mint `PublishedCommit`.** It returns a plain enum. `PublishedCommit`'s constructor stays private to storage and is reachable only from storage's own `commit()` after `SealOutcome::Committed`.
167	- **The callback cannot bypass the S6 checkpoint.** It is unreachable except from inside `seal_under_append_lock`, after the checkpoint and after witness COMMITTED.
168	- **The association values come from the owners.** `SealBinding` is constructed only by security; storage reads the 13 values from it rather than asserting them — which is the plan's own stated requirement, now enforced by construction.

170	**Release / REV cleanup.** On a failed final checkpoint with SEAL already durable: latch fail-stop on the session; do **not** invoke the callback; return `Refused{sealDurable: true}`; security releases L4 on return; storage aborts its evidence transaction; then the host — with L4 released — calls a fresh `security::record_revocation(...)` which takes a new L3 journal transaction and then L4. Storage maps it to a typed storage error; host maps it to the D9 refusal and, **after releasing the operation lease**, routes a lifecycle `close_generation` that takes the fence and appends TERMINAL. 176	### 4.2 CR-08 — refined, and one new fact
177	
178	Your objection is correct and the answer is narrower than I implied. Three source facts settle it:
179	
180	1. The chain is `prev_sha256[k] = SHA256(body_sha256[k-1] ‖ (k-1))` (v1 §5.4 DDL comment), and `body_sha256[k] = SHA256(body[k])` is a **separate column**. Rewriting an interior body and fixing the successor's `prev_sha256` leaves the tail's `body_sha256` unchanged.
181	2. The contract says so itself: *"Hash chain. Tamper-evidence for audit, **not tamper-proof**; the chain head is in the witness."*
182	3. **New and load-bearing:** in the `PENDING n+1, tail n` state the witness's `bodySha256` names the record that was *never appended*. The prior `COMMITTED n` witness has been overwritten. **During a PENDING append the carrier has no live witnessed anchor for its durable prefix at all.** (The reconciliation table confirms the reading: the ADVANCE row compares hashes at `PENDING n = tail n`; the REVERT row at `PENDING n+1, tail n` compares nothing.)
183	
184	So a walk "through k" proves nothing on its own, and neither does a walk to the tail when the witness is PENDING-ahead.
185	
186	**The custody-qualified retained anchor that suffices is the SC-TRUST high-water record** `{project, grantGeneration, lastSeq, tailSha256}`. It is written under the **fence** at operation start and end, is never written under a lease, and is **not** overwritten by a PENDING witness. That is the only retained anchor that survives a later in-flight append.
187	
188	> **Confirm-an-earlier-receipt predicate (read-only, no repair, no waiting):**
189	>
190	> Let `A` = the private association, `k = A.journalSeq`, `t` = observed journal tail, `W` = live witness, `H` = SC-TRUST high-water for `(A.journalCarrierDigest, A.grantGeneration)`.
191	>
192	> **Common checks (all required):** carrier naming — `W.projectKeyDigest == A.journalCarrierDigest` and `W.grantGeneration == A.grantGeneration`; contiguity of seq 1..t; chain consistency `prev_sha256[j] == SHA256(body_sha256[j-1] ‖ (j-1))` for all `j` in 2..t and `body_sha256[j] == SHA256(body[j])`; record join at `k` — `record_type == SEAL`, `body_sha256[k] == A.journalBodySha256`, `operationRef == A.operationRef`, record `runId == A.runId`; and `t >= H.lastSeq` (a lower tail is F22 quarantine, never a confirmation).
193	>
194	> **Anchor selection:**
195	> - `W` is **COMMITTED n** with `n == t` and `W.bodySha256 == body_sha256[t]` → anchor is the tail. Confirm for any `k ≤ t`.
196	> - `W` is **PENDING n == t** with `W.bodySha256 == body_sha256[t]` (journal durable, witness not yet advanced) → the witness still anchors the tail. **Confirm for any `k ≤ t`.** Report `witnessPendingAdvanceable` as diagnosis; perform no ADVANCE.
197	> - `W` is **PENDING n == t+1** (append not durable) → **no tail anchor exists.** Fall back to the SC-TRUST floor: confirm only if `k ≤ H.lastSeq` **and** `body_sha256[H.lastSeq] == H.tailSha256`. If `k > H.lastSeq`, the outcome is **`unknown`** — not confirmed, and explicitly **not** invalidated. The earlier committed prefix is never falsely invalidated by a newer PENDING append.
198	> - Any other witness state (`COMMITTED n > t`, equal seq different hash, non-adjacent PENDING, foreign carrier, malformed) → F20/F21/F22 quarantine/indeterminate.
199	>
200	> **No repair, no waiting:** no INIT/REVERT/ADVANCE, no witness write, no high-water raise, no lock acquisition, no wait on the writer.
201	>
202	> **Honest bound:** the conclusion class is **`confirmed-under-retained-custody`**, never "cryptographically proven". This establishes retained-carrier internal consistency plus non-rollback below the last *observed* floor. It does **not** detect a coherent whole-carrier rewrite performed while no operation was running with the witness and floor rewritten consistently — precisely the limit §5.4 "Detection bound (honest)" and §5.5 already state. Do not let the recovery prose imply more than the carrier provides.

254	### 5.2 Schema generation and SDK reuse
255	
256	- **One owner per contract, generation is downstream.** `schemas/registry.json` must key each entry by the schema document's **`raw-artifact`** digest — identity §3 defines `raw-artifact` as "raw SHA256 of the exact retained artifact bytes… a **complete registered schema document**". That is the join that prevents a schema change being laundered through a regenerated binding: the registry row names the exact document bytes, the generator closure and options, the output targets, and the **semantic validator owner** separately.
257	- **Generated types are shape, never admission.** Identity §3's exact-integer, duplicate-key and lexical-admission laws are the real gate; a generated Rust/TS carrier that parses through a permissive JSON layer has not admitted anything. The registry row must state, per target, whether the generated code performs exact admission (it must not be assumed to).
258	- **SDK reuse — decidable now, and the answer is "no shared SDK yet".** The two providers do not share a protocol: different majors (2 vs 3), different capability token sets, different context records (`TypeScriptNativeContextV2` vs `NativeContextV2`), different toolchain identity records. The only genuinely shared surfaces are the four identity tokens (`source-identity-snapshot2`, `plan-identity-plan2`, `fact-identity-fact2`, `coverage-v3`) and `HelloV3`/`HelloAckV3` framing. Those are already owned by `opensip-contracts` (Rust) and the generated TS protocol binding. **Recommendation: do not add a provider SDK package.** Revisit only if a third provider appears or the majors converge; the plan's "compare actual protocol obligations first" is satisfied — the comparison has now been done and it comes out negative.
259	
260	### 5.3 Report asset closure owner — a real gap (**CR-24**)
261	
262	`closure2.kind` is a **closed enum with no report/asset member**. The implementation plan's asset policy says a release "must fail assembly if its selected report asset closure is missing or incompatible" — using "closure" without saying which mechanism. There are only three consistent options and the plan must pick one:
263	
264	| Option | Cost |
265	|---|---|
266	| (a) Add a `kind` member | Widens a **closed identity vocabulary** for a presentation artifact; schema-major decision; drags report assets into `closure2` identity for no semantic benefit |
267	| (b) Carry assets inside an existing kind's tree | Misuses `provider`/`adapter` semantics; the assets are not an analyzer |
268	| **(c) Release artifact, not a `closure2`** | **Recommended.** |
269	
270	**Recommended (c):** the report asset bundle is a **release artifact** with its own manifest of exact asset bytes and a catalog `releases[].artifacts[]` row (`platform`-independent or per-platform as the bundle requires), verified by digest at assembly and again at load by `crates/reporting/src/assets.rs`. It is **not** a `closure2`, never enters identity, Run hashes, the native context or any semantic digest. Failure to verify at render time is the existing required-delivery operational failure (`DELIVERY.REQUIRED_FAILED`, exit 4) — never a silent degraded report. This keeps `assets.rs`'s stated responsibility ("versioned built report assets supplied by the signed release closure") truthful while leaving the closed identity vocabulary alone, and it needs no new signing scheme, consistent with the plan's own constraint.
271

273	
274	You asked me to separate these, and most of them can.
275

277	- TS package manager and lock topology (behaviour: independent lane install/build, no cross-lane scripts or toolchains, offline input materialisation — build-lane table + enforcement item 3).

329	## 7. New findings this pass
330	
331	- **CR-23 (medium-high, defect).** No fault case covers **an observer latch during or after the evidence-commit syscall**. F19 is scoped to "after SEAL but before evidence commit" and concludes `uncommitted`; F12 covers a commit-syscall error without a concurrent latch; F26 covers revocation after a *confirmed* commit. The gap in between would mislabel an already-linearised or durability-undetermined attempt as `uncommitted`. Required: (i) record a `linearizationPoint` at callback entry — a latch at or after it can never yield `refused`; (ii) commit confirmed → `committed`, with the latch refusing only *subsequent* effects, producing `committed-delivery-failed`; (iii) commit error or unconfirmed barrier → `durability-undetermined` with ExecutionId, no write retry, latch does not convert it to `uncommitted`; (iv) REV appended after L4 release must record the SEAL `journalSeq` and its evidence outcome so a later reader cannot read REV-after-SEAL as a refusal; (v) state plainly that the S6 observer bound bounds *admitting new effects*, not aborting an in-flight syscall.

22	  BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'grant journal is append-only'); END;
23	CREATE TRIGGER gj_seq_contiguous BEFORE INSERT ON grant_journal
24	  BEGIN
25	    SELECT CASE WHEN NEW.seq <> (SELECT COALESCE(MAX(seq), 0) + 1 FROM grant_journal WHERE grantGeneration = NEW.grantGeneration)

27	    SELECT CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM grant_journal WHERE grantGeneration = NEW.grantGeneration AND record_type = 'TERMINAL')

29	    SELECT CASE WHEN NEW.seq = 9007199254740991 AND NEW.record_type <> 'TERMINAL'
30	      THEN RAISE(ABORT, 'grant journal seq 9007199254740991 is the reserved terminal slot; roll the grant generation') END;
31	  END;

1234 ## S16. Existing prototype users and local-state transition (DR-130)

421	## S6. Live revocation (AR-05)
422	
423	Trust epoch `{rootVersion, indexSnapshotVersion, revocationVersion,
424	permissionPolicyDigest}` is captured at operation start. **Authority
425	checkpoint:** every brokered effect request re-reads the epoch under the
426	journal append lock before its intent record. **Observer:** a tick every 5 s
427	reads the counter; if the last successful read is older than 10 s or the read
428	fails, the observer appends `REV(observer-fail-stop)` and cancels. These bounds
429	are implementation qualification obligations under OS scheduling assumptions
430	using `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` (Linux) / `mach_continuous_time` (macOS); they are not a
431	wall-clock guarantee inside a stopped process. A stopped process emits no
432	effects; on resume its first checkpoint or tick observes the stall and fail-
433	stops before any further effect.
434	
435	The observation predicate revokes on a higher counter whose entries name the
436	closure (release, signing key, namespace, catalog snapshot) or on a policy
437	digest change that removes a required grant; unrelated changes are recorded as
438	drift; a lower counter never revokes (rollback is detected by the floor rules).
439	
440	**Linearization** is under the single journal append lock: after `REV` no
441	`RA`, intent, commit or `SEAL` is appended, and no brokered effect commits.
442	Commit records carry `postimageSha256`. At `REV(trust-revoked)` the host
443	attempts rollback of reversible completed effects **only where the current
444	bytes equal the committed postimage**; a mismatch is `rollbackBlocked`
445	(user-modified since commit, never overwritten), an unreadable target is
446	`indeterminate`. Irreversible completed effects and effects under
447	`REV(policy|operator)` are disclosed as completed. The `CLN` record lists every
448	residual. Cancellation is bounded: refuse further requests (0 s), protocol
449	Cancel (2 s), SIGTERM (3 s), SIGKILL of the process group and reap (5 s),
450	scratch cleanup under the lease; total 10 s under the same qualification
451	standing. **Unconfined children** (repository code under S10) are not brokered
452	effects: they are cancelled within the bound and disclosed, and their external
453	effects before the kill are not enumerable. No confinement is claimed.
454	
455	**Three different SEAL boundaries, not one.** (1) `linearize` is an abstract
456	brokered-effect schedule over a grant journal. Its all-zero `run3:` SEAL id is
457	a **fixture** token for that schedule. It is not a product host, not native
458	fact authority, and not `identity-model.v3.close_run`. (2)
459	`admit_seal_run_id_prefix` is narrow `run3` pattern dispatch. It admits a
460	well-formed non-fixture prefix and refuses `run2` and the fixture id. It does
461	not replay a graph. (3) `admit_analysis_seal` is the public reference SEAL of
462	an analysis Run: current `JournalRecord` fields (`recordSchema` 3, closed
463	required members), then `identity-model.v3.close_run` on the supplied retained
464	graph, then byte-equal RunId comparison. Owner-only `open_run_closure` is not
465	that boundary. A well-formed `run3:` that is not the replayed identity refuses
466	`SEAL_RUN_ID_MISMATCH`. Schema-2 journals remain frozen historical bytes and
467	are not read as 3. Mixed prefixes refuse. There is no `run[23]` alternation.
468	Revocation still blocks schedule-SEAL after `REV`. Grant/root schema-2
469	documents are a different axis. This dispatch does not change lease modes,
470	lock order, or permission-truth-table effect values. Proof
471	`executionInputsDigest` is required by identity reconstruct; this unit does
472	not mint it.
473	
474	## S7. Leases and lock order (AR-14)
475	
476	The current security schema bundle declares every array's `x-opensip-order`
477	under identity §3. Namespace lists use strictly unique raw UTF-8 locator order;
478	execution-grant owner records use strictly unique `ownerKey` order. Public code
479	sets use strictly unique UTF-8 order. Other arrays are explicit sequences unless
480	their owning schema states a stricter order: journal revisions, lock traces,
481	release steps, signature entries and observations are never silently sorted.
482	This collection-admission law does not change the security metadata canonical
483	profile or its immutable historical schemas.
484	
485	| Level | Lock | Carrier | Blocking |
486	|---|---|---|---|
487	| 0 | lifecycle fence | `<installRoot>/lifecycle.fence`, flock LOCK_EX | bounded wait 5 s, then `PROJECT.BUSY` |
488	| 1 | project writer lease | `<namespace>/writer.lease`, LOCK_EX\|LOCK_NB | never |
489	| 2 | project reader lease | `<namespace>/readers.lease`, LOCK_SH\|LOCK_NB (readers); LOCK_EX\|LOCK_NB (EXCLUSIVE) | never |
490	| 3 | ledger transaction | SQLite WAL; writers BEGIN IMMEDIATE, busy_timeout 0; readers read a committed snapshot | never for readers |
491	| 4 | journal append lock | in-process mutex | bounded, in-process |
492	
493	Modes: `SHARED-READ` (any number; queries, rendering, doctor, read-only
494	agents), `APPEND-WRITE` (one; analysis, import, baseline pin; publishes only
495	new immutable objects and ledger rows, never deletes or rewrites bytes a reader
496	may reference), `EXCLUSIVE` (GC, purge, migration, repair apply; nothing else
497	held). Readers never block a writer; a second writer or an EXCLUSIVE request
498	gets `PROJECT.BUSY` at once, releases the fence, and may retry outside the
499	fence with backoff 1/2/4/8/15 s within a 30 s budget. Laws: no lease without
500	the fence; no waiting for a lease; no waiting for the fence while holding a
501	lease (operation end releases the lease first); no upgrade; trust state is
502	written only under the fence and never under a lease; GC census is a
503	LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB probe under the fence and a busy probe means retain.
504	
505	**One-writer refinement (identity-and-evidence §5).** "Exactly one per-project
506	writer holds the lifecycle lease through admission, evaluation and commit" is
507	the APPEND-WRITE mode: exactly one append writer, coexisting with any number of
508	immutable-snapshot readers that never wait on it. The EXCLUSIVE mode is the
509	refinement for migration, purge, GC and repair apply, which need a reader
510	census (the LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB probe) because they may remove or rewrite bytes a
511	reader could reference. There is no contradiction with the identity contract:
512	readers are invisible to the writer's commit order and the writer is invisible
513	to readers' snapshots. Exact selectors: `<namespace>/writer.lease` LOCK_EX|NB
514	is the identity contract's "lifecycle lease"; `<namespace>/readers.lease`
515	LOCK_SH|NB is its "consistent committed snapshot"; `<installRoot>/lifecycle.fence`
516	is its "global trust admission and revocation lock order".
517	
518	**Namespaces.** Every project lease names a namespace from the host namespace
519	registry (ProjectId ↔ namespace locator, identity §5); a lease on an
520	unregistered namespace is a violation, never an implicit registration
521	(`lease-on-an-unregistered-namespace-is-refused-negative`). Namespaces are
522	independent: a writer in one never blocks a writer in another.
523	
524	**Core-transition lock set (decided; SHOULD-6).** `core update|repair|rollback`
525	and `store migrate|rollback` change install-level state, while EXCLUSIVE is a
526	per-namespace lease. The mechanism is a composition, not a new flock mode:
527	
528	1. The install-wide fence (level 0) is held for the **whole** transition, not
529	   only for lease acquisition; no project operation can be admitted meanwhile.
530	2. The affected namespace set is enumerated from the registry by
531	   `core_transition_affected_namespaces` (never from user input or a directory
532	   listing): **all registered namespaces** when the from/to state schema differ
533	   or a store is re-selected (`core rollback`, `store migrate|rollback`);
534	   **no namespace** for a same-schema `core update` or `core repair`, because
535	   the selected core closure is an immutable generation, running project
536	   operations keep their pinned generation and re-check trust at their S6
537	   checkpoints, and nothing they reference is rewritten.
538	3. EXCLUSIVE is taken on each affected namespace in namespace-locator byte
539	   order, non-blocking and all-or-nothing: the first busy namespace releases
540	   every acquired lease in reverse order, releases the fence, reports
541	   `PROJECT.BUSY` naming that namespace and its holders, and the retry is the
542	   ordinary backoff outside the fence.
543	4. The `InstallationTransitionJournalV1` (S9.2) names the exact lease set and is
544	   written only after every lease is held: in the lock model the
545	   `transition-journal` action is lawful only under the fence, only after
546	   `core-transition-acquire` succeeded, and only naming exactly the held set
547	   (`transition-journal-*` cases). Crash
548	   recovery runs as the first act under the next fence acquisition, before any
549	   admission, over the S9.2 recovery table (which defers to the S9 footprint
550	   table for store operations), and re-acquires exactly the journaled
551	   set; flock leases die with the process, so no stale lease survives. A
552	   namespace registered after the intent cannot exist (registration needs the
553	   fence); finding one is `MIGRATION.CORRUPT`.
554	5. Leases are released in reverse order, then the fence. The fence cannot be
555	   released while transition leases are held.
556	
557	Ordinary component `install`/`update` publish new immutable generations under
558	the fence alone and never revoke a generation a live operation pins (removal
559	is GC census only). GC iterates registered namespaces and treats a busy
560	namespace as retain, never as refusal. Reference `lease_schedule` (registry,
561	`core-transition-acquire|release`, `transition-journal`),
562	`core_transition_affected_namespaces`; cases `core-transition-*`,
563	`transition-journal-*`, `two-namespaces-are-independent-*`.
564	
565	Command → lease map (workflows command inventory):
566	
567	| Lease | Commands |
568	|---|---|
569	| none (fence only, no project lock) | `install`, `update` (component generations), `trust refresh|import|recovery-challenge|recovery-import`, ordinary payload import, `doctor` / `trust doctor` / `store status` (report-only, no write) |
570	| SHARED-READ | `query`, `recommend`, `baseline show`, `policy show|test`, `candidates`, `inspect`, `review brief`, `repair preview`, `agent serve` reads, `doctor` project checks |
571	| APPEND-WRITE | `opensip` default, `analyze`, `fit`, `audit`, `import`, `baseline adopt|export|upgrade`, `policy init`, `waive`, `review join`, `test run`, `native prepare`, `repair verify` |
572	| EXCLUSIVE (one namespace) | `repair apply` (S10.1 authorization), `repair recover --apply-recovery` (S10.2 authorization; inspection alone is SHARED-READ), `purge`, `store gc` per namespace (busy = retain) |
573	| core-transition lock set (fence held + EXCLUSIVE on every affected registered namespace) | `core update`, `core repair`, `core rollback`, `store migrate`, `store rollback` |
574	
575	Trust recovery deliberately takes no project lease: it mutates SC-TRUST only,
576	under the fence, and a project operation that starts afterwards observes the
577	new floor at its trust instant.
578	
579	## S8. Platform population and admission (AR-06)
580	
581	Selected support population (D-367 design selection) and its qualification
582	lanes (security v8 §8.7 classes). **One machine platform vocabulary (MUST-2):**
583	the `Platform id` column is the only machine identity, used unchanged as the
584	signed `PlatformProfileSetV1` key, the `platform` of every admission record,
585	`RepoExecutionGrantV2.platformId` and its truth-table key, the native matrix
586	`platformFamilies` (native §1.1), the workflow test-execution `platformId` and
587	the qualification-gate `platformFamilies`. The `Display alias` column is human
588	rendering only: an alias presented as a platform refuses
589	`NT-TCB-PROFILE-UNQUALIFIED:platform-display-alias-not-machine-id:<id>`, a
590	profile set keyed by one is schema-invalid and refuses
591	`NT-TCB-PROFILE-UNQUALIFIED:PROFILE_SET_KEY_NOT_MACHINE_ID:<id>`, and a grant carrying one
592	refuses `GRANT.PLATFORM_DISPLAY_ALIAS_NOT_MACHINE_ID:<id>`.
593	`PROFILE_SET_KEY_NOT_MACHINE_ID` is **not** a public `DomainDetailCode` and must not be
594	registered as one: it is a **subject sub-detail** of the registered
595	`NT-TCB-PROFILE-UNQUALIFIED`, in the same position as
596	`platform-display-alias-not-machine-id`, `MACOS_MAJOR_26` and `DISTRO_SERIES` (S12). Lane names keep their
597	historical spelling; historical documents that use the aliases are unchanged.
598	The checker sweep
599	`one-machine-platform-vocabulary-joins-profile-set-admission-grant-native-matrix-and-workflow-schema`
600	admits every id through `platform_admit` and then a grant carrying that same
601	id, and checks the four id sets are equal across the units.
602	
603	| Platform id | Display alias | Population | Lane |
604	|---|---|---|---|
605	| `macos-aarch64` | macos-arm64 | macOS 15 and 26, Apple silicon, sealed system volume, SIP on, APFS install root | `macos-15` |
606	| `macos-x86_64` | macos-x86_64 | macOS 15 and 26, Intel, same predicates | `macos-15-intel` |
607	| `linux-x86_64-gnu` | linux-x86_64 | Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, Canonical-signed kernels on supported lines/flavors, ext4/xfs/btrfs install root | `ubuntu-24.04` |
608	| `linux-aarch64-gnu` | linux-arm64 | Ubuntu 24.04 LTS on arm64, same | `ubuntu-24.04-arm` |
609	
610	The signed `PlatformProfileSetV1` carries, per platform, the release-measured
611	identities from its lane (`EXACT-MEASURED` tier) and the supported baseline:
612	macOS supported majors with minimum builds; Linux supported kernel lines and
613	flavors. An identity inside the baseline but not measured is admitted at the
614	`BASELINE-ATTESTED` tier with its identity recorded as drift (never allow/
615	refuse). Security predicates are identical at both tiers: sealed root and SIP
616	(macOS); Ubuntu build string, kernel package installed by the Ubuntu maintainer,
617	archive key digest, mount-namespace stability, install-root filesystem; under
618	`secure-boot-lockdown`, Secure Boot on, lockdown not `none`, UEFI signer
619	present. A measured profile labelled with a lane outside its platform's lane
620	list is unqualified. Outside the population (other distributions, self-built
621	kernels, unsupported lines/flavors, non-listed filesystems, Windows) the core
622	refuses rather than degrades.
623	
624	Honest limits, disclosed in every admission record: the baseline tier admits
625	identities no lane measured and does not detect a hostile kernel;
626	`package-db-declared` provides no boot attestation; macOS Full vs Reduced
627	Security is not distinguished at launch and boot policy is unobservable on
628	hosted lanes. Case values in the reference are placeholders, not measurements.
629	
630	## S9. Stage transition, schema bridge and floor continuity (AR-14)
631	
632	Bridge. Stage 1: root readers {1}, state decoder v1, TR-REPAIR typed absence,
633	`kernelAttestationKeys` empty. Stage 2: root readers {1, 2}, state decoders
634	`state-decoder.v1` (read-only migration source) and `state-decoder.v2`
635	(writer); schema-2 roots may carry an active TR-REPAIR (threshold ≥ 2, keys ≥
636	threshold + 1, namespaces present, no reuse of root keys) and up to 8 kernel
637	attestation keys (no reuse of root keys). Ordered release: (1) the stage-2 core
638	ships under the schema-1 catalog, so every stage-1 install updates by its
639	ordinary path; (2) root N+1 with schema 2 is signed by root-N keys and its own
640	keys; (3) stage-1 cores refuse N+1 typed and keep N until it expires; stage-2
641	cores accept it by the dual reader; (4) state migration 1→2 runs under
642	EXCLUSIVE. Both stages keep the metadata profile of S2.
643	
644	Migration writes a `migrating` root: PREPARING → PREPARED → (old store fenced
645	`RESTORED`) → COMMITTED → final rename. Recovery from the durable footprint
646	only: absent = nothing to do; PREPARING or PREPARED with the old store unfenced
647	= abort; PREPARED with the old store fenced = resume from step 3; COMMITTED =
648	resume the final rename; final and migrating coexisting, or unknown state =
649	quarantine `MIGRATION.CORRUPT`. Floors (`rootVersion`, `indexSnapshotVersion`,
650	`revocationVersion`, `evalHighWater`, `lastAccepted`, `recoveryEpochSerial`)
651	copy forward into the new store; the boot anchor and any pending challenge do
652	not; roles re-establish by the PRESENT event over the embedded chain. A new core
653	whose embedded chain does not reach the accepted root refuses
654	`ROOT.FLOOR_ABOVE_CORE`. Rollback inside the 30 d window re-selects the retained
655	old store with floors set to the maximum of both stores; it refuses when the
656	new store accepted a root the old core cannot verify (schema or chain reach). A
657	poisoned floor is not lowered by migration or rollback; only S4.5 lowers it.
658	
659	### S9.1 Root schema 2 and signed profile-set binding (design, closed)
660	
661	**The product admission boundary is `security/security-lifecycle.schemas.v1.json $.schemas.RootV1`
662	and `$.schemas.RootV2`, reached only through `admit_root_document`.** No other document admits a
663	root. Root **schema 1** *preserves the rule set* of the historical
664	`docs/coop/completion/security-schemas.v8/root.schema.json`, which remains the immutable
665	**rule source** and is not a second gate. The successor is not byte-equivalent to it and is not
666	meant to be: every successor pattern ends with the strict `(?![\s\S])` assertion, where the
667	retained v8 patterns end with a bare `$`. Under Draft 2020-12 a bare `$` matches before a final
668	newline, so a root whose `indexOrigin.url` or whose role `namespaces` item carries a trailing
669	newline is admitted by the historical bytes and **refused** by the product boundary
670	(`PAYLOAD-NOT-ADMISSIBLE`, detail `ROOT.SCHEMA_SHAPE`, exit 2). That is the intended successor
671	semantics — the discipline is universal across the product-successor schema documents — and it is
672	regressed through the actual host gate, not through the schema alone, by
673	`root-schema-cases.v1.json` cases
674	`schema-1-root-with-a-trailing-newline-index-origin-url-refuses-at-the-product-boundary` and
675	`...-role-namespace-...`. Preserved semantic rules of schema 1 (`RootV1`: TR-REPAIR typed absence,
676	`kernelAttestationKeys` exactly `[]`, `recoveryAuthority` 5–16 keys at
677	threshold ≥ 3, disjoint from `rootKeys`). Root **schema 2** (`RootV2`) is the
678	exact extension recipe, and nothing else changes:
679	
680	| Field | Schema 1 | Schema 2 |

476	whose concurrence that supersession names (Semantic, Evidence, storage, operability, lifecycle,
477	DR-105 security/platform, V1 coordinator) are architecture roles delegated to the pair by D-367;
478	this contract records their concurrence. Overturn restores the three prohibitions for new writes
479	and freezes written records, as v11 states.

481	### 5.4 Grant-journal carrier encoding (closes ID-DEP-P5, ID-DEP-P6)
482	
483	One SQLite database per project under the host-owned project state namespace,
484	`grant-journal.sqlite`, opened WAL with `synchronous=FULL`; foreign keys on. Written only by the
485	DR-105 host broker holding the project/operation lock (the same lock the paired draft's
486	`project_selection` uses). Lock order when both are needed: install-root lifecycle lock first,
487	then project/operation lock; released in reverse; a writer never blocks on the lifecycle lock
488	while holding the project lock.
489	
490	```sql
491	CREATE TABLE grant_journal (
492	  grantGeneration INTEGER NOT NULL,          -- grant generation (carrier); NOT the lifecycle install generation
493	  seq          INTEGER NOT NULL,             -- strictly increasing per generation
494	  record_type  TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (record_type IN
495	                 ('GRANT','NARROW','EXPIRY','RA','RCI','RCO','ICI','ICO','REV','CLN','AUD',
496	                  'CHECKPOINT','MIGRATION','TERMINAL')),
497	  operation_ref TEXT   NOT NULL,             -- operation identity value rides DR-006; structure only
498	  request_ref  TEXT,                         -- broker request id (RA/RCI/RCO/ICI/ICO)
499	  token        TEXT,                         -- PT-* on grant-bearing records
500	  body         TEXT    NOT NULL,             -- opensip-metadata-canonical.1 bytes, domain opensip.metadata.journal.1
501	  body_sha256  TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (length(body_sha256) = 64),
502	  prev_sha256  TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (length(prev_sha256) = 64), -- chain: sha256 of previous record's body_sha256||seq
503	  install_generation_id TEXT,                -- lifecycle generation the grant binds (ID-DEP-P2, recorded identity)
504	  manifest_digest TEXT CHECK (manifest_digest IS NULL OR length(manifest_digest) = 64),
505	  platform     TEXT CHECK (platform IN ('macos-arm64','macos-x86_64','linux-x86_64','linux-arm64') OR platform IS NULL),
506	  CHECK (record_type <> 'GRANT' OR (install_generation_id IS NOT NULL AND manifest_digest IS NOT NULL AND platform IS NOT NULL)),
507	  PRIMARY KEY (grantGeneration, seq)
508	) WITHOUT ROWID;
509	CREATE TRIGGER gj_no_update BEFORE UPDATE ON grant_journal
510	  BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'grant journal is append-only'); END;
511	CREATE TRIGGER gj_no_delete BEFORE DELETE ON grant_journal
512	  BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'grant journal is append-only'); END;
513	CREATE TABLE carrier_quarantine (              -- carrierQuarantineRecord: external, non-appending
514	  grantGeneration INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
515	  reason     TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (reason IN ('uncertainTailLoss','witnesslessRestore')),
516	  observed_tail_seq INTEGER,
517	  body       TEXT NOT NULL
518	);
519	CREATE TABLE carrier_capacity_pause (          -- capacityPause: proven tail intact
520	  grantGeneration INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
521	  proven_tail_seq INTEGER NOT NULL,
522	  reserved_terminal_slot INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1
523	);
524	```

526	Rules bound to the schema:
527	
528	- **Grant generation.** A per-project integer starting at 1 that advances only at grant-generation
529	  closure (a REV of the whole generation, or project purge, per `terminalization`); it is not the
530	  lifecycle install generation. Every `GRANT` record binds `install_generation_id`,
531	  `manifest_digest` and `platform`, so a grant is bound to the recorded component bytes
532	  (ID-DEP-P2) and cannot authorize a different generation or manifest
533	  (FC-CROSS-GENERATION-REPLAY, FC-WRONG-MANIFEST).
534	- **Sequence.** Inside one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction: `seq = COALESCE(MAX(seq),0)+1` for the
535	  grant generation, then insert, then commit. The record is ORDERED when and only when the commit is
536	  durable (`synchronous=FULL` in WAL mode syncs the WAL at each commit). Nothing external is
537	  initiated before the RCI/ICI commit returns.
538	- **Terminal marker.** `TERMINAL` is appended by the first of {projectPurge, grantGenerationClosure}
539	  on a healthy carrier; a later one is a no-op (`terminalization.openHealthy`). Capacity pause
540	  keeps one reserved slot for it.
541	- **Witness.** After each durable commit the writer updates the SC-TRUST high-water witness
542	  `{project, grantGeneration, lastSeq, tailSha256}`. Restore compares: `witness.lastSeq >
543	  MAX(seq)` → `uncertainTailLoss` quarantine; no witness → `witnesslessRestore` quarantine; either
544	  way `failClosedNoAppend` and continuation only on a new generation. A stale witness (lower
545	  than the tail) is safe and is advanced.
546	- **Recovery.** Replay from the last `CHECKPOINT` record; `RA` without successor →
547	  CANCELED-BY-RECOVERY; `RCI` without outcome → run the class inverse and record `CLN`; `ICI`
548	  without outcome → `ICO` INDETERMINATE (`irreversibleBoundary.indeterminateOutcome`); `REV`
549	  read first. The FX-4 crash matrix enumerates every write and fsync boundary of this schema
550	  on both platforms.
551	- **Secrets.** Secret VALUES never enter `body`; handles do (file 03).
552	- **Hash chain.** Tamper-evidence for audit, not tamper-proof; the chain head is in the witness.
553	
554	## 6. DR-105 and DR-114: joint-owner decisions
555	
556	### 6.1 Execution mode (ID-DEP-P10) — DECIDED
557	
558	The architecture preview admits components in **child-process mode only**. `in-host-process`
559	is refused at admission (RJ-6 RESERVED_FIELD_POPULATED if a manifest asks for it; no token).

1 # Implementation boundaries and build plan
22 ## Admission and authoritative commit
24 ### Decision: require independently minted prerequisites at the storage boundary
81 ### Security/storage ownership and the final commit gate
146 ### Publication sequence and lock discipline
203 ### Failure and recovery account
223 ### Private recovery record and storage-generation binding
296 ### Witness-aware publication and read-only recovery
385 ### Ordered failure matrix
434 ### Required API and fault-injection checks
458 ## Build, generation and dependency rules
460 ### Independently selectable build lanes
517 ### Enforcement and verification
547 ## Implementation milestones after design acceptance
573 ## Implementation coverage account
619 ### Command routing
669 ### Qualification routing
725 ## Tooling decision matrix
754 ## Author verification
774 ## Questions reserved for actual Claude

81	### Security/storage ownership and the final commit gate
82	
83	`begin_journal_txn(session: CommitSession)` consumes the session and returns an
84	opaque `JournalWriteTxn` owned by security. It owns the live session and its
85	operation lease, has no public SQL/write/checkpoint method and is non-cloneable.
86	It does not borrow a session that a later call must move. Storage holds this
87	opaque transaction while acquiring its own non-waiting level-3 ledger transaction.
88	Failure of that second acquisition calls the security-owned consuming abort path.
89	
90	`JournalSealBinding` is also defined and privately constructed in security,
91	not in the inert contracts crate. It exposes read-only actual carrier/generation,
92	SEAL sequence/body digest, operationRef and replayed Run identity. It is evidence
93	of that append, never a reusable effect grant. Storage owns the remaining receipt
94	and inventory values and assembles the thirteen-field association by checking
95	both owners' exact joins; security does not manufacture storage's receipt counter
96	or receipt bytes. Neither raw transaction handles nor the append mutex escape.
97	
98	The security-owned `seal_under_append_lock` consumes `JournalWriteTxn`, borrows
99	an evaluator-minted `ReplayedRun`, and owns the entire checkpoint/witness sequence.
100	It uses a two-phase storage adapter, whose concrete implementation and ledger
101	connection stay private to storage:
102	
103	1. After the SEAL/witness is durable, an at-most-once staging callback receives
104	   the opaque `JournalSealBinding`, validates its joins and inserts the exact
105	   receipt/association in the already-open evidence transaction. It returns an
106	   owned prepared-ledger-commit adapter. This phase may fail without issuing an
107	   evidence commit; it must not commit or publish by itself.
108	2. Security rechecks epoch/freshness and atomically admits commitment only if the
109	   observer's fail-stop latch has not won. It then consumes the adapter's one
110	   commit method. All payload admission, association construction and SQL staging
111	   precede this gate; the method performs only the prepared commit and barriers.
112	
113	The adapter trait is owned by security, which has no dependency on storage;
114	its implementation is storage-private. No authority-bearing type lives in
115	contracts merely to permit another crate to construct private fields. The trait
116	is an operational collaboration among trusted host modules, not a sandbox for
117	arbitrary downstream implementations. Storage's public facade accepts neither
118	an external adapter nor an external `SealOutcome`; callers cannot mint
119	`PublishedCommit` by returning a fabricated enum. The pure evaluator receives no
120	callback, port or mutable store handle.
121	
122	The observer latches fail-stop outside the append mutex when a check fails or
123	staleness exceeds S6's bound. A single atomic attempt state arbitrates latch versus
124	commit admission: a latch winning while preparing prevents the gate; a successful
125	prepare→commit-admitted transition wins before the commit syscall. An observer
126	latching after admission blocks subsequent effects but cannot undo a syscall or
127	rewrite its outcome. A confirmed durable commit remains committed; an uncertain
128	commit/barrier remains durability-undetermined with ExecutionId and no automatic
129	write retry. This gate orders admission only and is not the durability point.
130	
131	On any end path, security returns a stopped session that still owns the operation
132	lease and admits cleanup only, with no further analysis/effect APIs. After level 4
133	and any still-open ledger transaction are released, the host uses that stopped
134	session to record pending REV/cleanup through a fresh lawful level-3→level-4 append
135	while the operation lease still protects cleanup. It then releases the lease and
136	performs the ordinary S7 end handoff. Capacity exhaustion instead returns typed
137	`CarrierCapacityExhausted {grantGeneration, provenTailSeq}` through storage to
138	`host/finalization.rs`; after cleanup and lease release, host routes the required
139	lifecycle rollover under the fence. Storage never calls lifecycle backwards.
140	
141	Drop is best-effort rollback/resource release if it runs; `mem::forget`, process
142	abort and stalled syscalls do not guarantee destructor execution. Those paths
143	must leave recovery evidence and an honest unavailable/busy result, not a claimed
144	cleanup success. This design does not infer OS cancellation bounds from Rust types.
145	
146	### Publication sequence and lock discipline
147	
148	1. Host obtains registered project/store admission and the required writer guard
149	   through lifecycle/security before source admission. The guard remains owned
150	   through evaluation and commit. Operational grants precede Plan construction;
151	   Plan grant descriptors never authorize effects.
152	2. Native/import admission and the pure evaluator reconstruct the complete Run.
153	   A failed reconstruction returns its typed failure without producing
154	   `ReplayedRun`. Explicit ephemeral analysis uses a separate non-authoritative
155	   result path and cannot call the durable commit facade.
156	3. Storage binds the two prerequisites and preflights exact replayable retention,
157	   pins and bounds. It writes verified immutable objects to private temporary
158	   files, satisfies file barriers, publishes digest-addressed objects and
159	   satisfies directory barriers. Failure leaves no acknowledged Run.
160	4. Prepare both carrier write transactions at level 3 in one fixed order:
161	   security grant-journal first, evidence ledger second, both non-waiting. If
162	   either acquisition fails, release the earlier transaction. Only then take
163	   the journal append checkpoint at level 4. It never holds level 4 while
164	   trying to acquire either level-3 transaction. No lease upgrade or new project/fence
165	   acquisition occurs inside this path. Existing S7 rules own earlier fence and
166	   lease acquisition/release and contention handling.
167	5. Under the journal checkpoint, security checks current custody, relevant trust
168	   epoch, observer freshness, grants and operation cancellation. The final
169	   SEAL/commit sequence must linearize with REV: no new SEAL or commit after REV.
170	   No slow replay, provider execution, network operation or discovery occurs
171	   while this final lock is held. A short-lived checkpoint is never serialized
172	   as a reusable authority token.
173	6. Publish the Run manifest, references, availability, authorized pins, exact
174	   receipt and private recovery association in one synchronous ledger
175	   transaction; satisfy all required durability barriers. Only then produce
176	   `PublishedCommit`. Required rendering/delivery follows commitment and cannot
177	   rewrite its Run.
178	
179	**Proposed journal/ledger crash join for review:** persist the validated SEAL
180	record before ledger commit while holding the final journal lock through the
181	ledger commit/barrier. Include a private recovery association in that ledger
182	transaction linking namespace, ExecutionId, RunId, inventory digest, store
183	generation and the exact journal generation/sequence/record digest. Its values
184	come from the actual two owners, not caller assertions. The association is local
185	operational metadata, excluded from semantic hashes, and adds no field to the
186	closed public receipt or JournalRecord schemas. SEAL alone is not a durable
187	receipt. A surviving SEAL with no committed ledger row is an uncommitted attempt.
188	`admit_analysis_seal` validates a record and its Run; it does not establish that
189	attempt’s durable commitment. F36 requires the orphan attempt to remain
190	uncommitted after later operations. A later, properly receipted attempt may
191	commit the same semantic RunId; its new ExecutionId/receipt establishes that
192	commit and never retroactively confirms the earlier attempt.
193	
194	This is a concrete proposed carrier join, not a claim that candidate25 already
195	specifies or implements that private table. Claude must check its compatibility
196	with the selected journal carrier, operationRef binding, recovery and bounded
197	revocation rules. The private record shape and ordered fault-injection plan below now make the
198	proposal concrete. Their carrier implementation/migration still requires review
199	and real execution before qualification.
200	If that review requires a normative amendment, freeze and review a successor;
201	do not silently edit the selected public schemas or weaken the existing laws.
202	
203	### Failure and recovery account
204	
205	| Interruption / refusal | Durable state and required behavior |

223	### Private recovery record and storage-generation binding
224	
225	The machine-readable [recovery plan](commit-recovery-plan.v1.json) owns the closed
226	`CommitRecoveryAssociationV1` schema and F00–F37 checkpoint inventory. This is a
227	local operational record, never a public request, authority token or extension
228	to a Run/receipt/journal wire schema. All 13 fields are required, with no nulls,
229	unknown members, implicit defaults, duplicate JSON keys or lossy numeric parsing.
230	JSON Schema checks shape; the exact lexical and cross-owner checks below still
231	apply. Merely constructing a schema-valid association grants nothing.
232	
233	Select a private `StoreGenerationBindingV1` with exactly `{schemaVersion: 1,
234	namespaceId, storeInstanceId, storeGeneration, stateSchema}`. `namespaceId` is the same exact
235	1–4096-character registered namespace used by the receipt; `storeInstanceId`
236	is 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters from 128 bits of OS randomness allocated
237	once at authorized store creation. `storeGeneration` is exactly the S9.2
238	admitted `currentStoreGeneration` (`I64NonNegative`), validated against the
239	transition intent’s `from/toStoreGeneration`; it is not a second counter.
240	`stateSchema` uses the owning security `$defs/StateSchema` domain, currently
241	`{1, 2}`. It widens only through an explicit reviewed successor of that owner
242	and supported-reader admission, never because a generic integer can encode it.
243	The binding is custody-protected store metadata; `storeGenerationDigest` is raw
244	SHA-256 of its canonical bytes, used only for local correlation. It is not a new
245	public H-domain, semantic identity or proof that a store is trusted. The active
246	security guard obtains this binding through an admitted handle and registry,
247	not from request fields. Randomness never enters the pure evaluator or Run hash.
248	
249	The binding survives ordinary restart, a same-store core update that preserves
250	the admitted state schema/store generation, and index rebuild.
251	A newly created/restored store instance receives a new storeInstanceId; an explicit
252	state-schema or store-generation transition publishes a new binding and retains
253	its authorized predecessor association. S9 validates the exact old/new
254	`(storeInstanceId, storeGeneration, stateSchema)` tuple against the transition
255	intent and current registry state. The random instance identity distinguishes
256	separately created/restored stores with coincident numeric generations; it never
257	replaces lifecycle generation checks or restores a backup’s local authority. Old commit rows keep their original digest. Historical
258	lookup follows an admitted migration lineage or reports unavailability; it never
259	rewrites old rows to pretend they were committed by the new instance. Portable
260	adoption is a fresh locally authorized attempt, not recovery of local authority
261	from a backup. Exact lineage validation belongs to lifecycle transitions under S9.
262	
263	Storage owns an append-only association table, inserted **in the same evidence
264	ledger transaction** as its receipt, Run references, availability and pins.
265	Primary key: `(storeGenerationDigest, namespaceId, executionId)`. Unique keys:
266	`(storeGenerationDigest, namespaceId, commitSequence)` and
267	`(journalCarrierDigest, grantGeneration, journalSeq)`. Keep low-level row insertion
268	private to the guarded commit facade. No `INSERT OR REPLACE`, mutation-on-read,
269	unchecked restore constructor or convenience API may bypass these invariants.
270	Public schema versions are unaffected by this private record's version 1.
271	
272	Map strings to binary-comparison SQL TEXT and counters within signed-i64 to SQL
273	INTEGER. `commitSequence` uses canonical decimal TEXT so uint64 receipt values
274	cannot overflow a signed SQLite integer; require an exact parse/range check and
275	compare numeric magnitude (length then bytes for canonical nonnegative decimals),
276	not lexical order alone or REAL conversion. The row's sequence value must equal
277	the selected receipt's numeric value. The public receipt remains numeric under
278	its own schema; this explicit private representation is not coercion at admission. The
279	SQL column also constrains text length to 1..20. One private ledger accessor
280	owns exact decoding and length-then-binary-byte ordering; raw SQL handles remain
281	private. No bare lexical `MAX`/`ORDER BY`, `CAST(... AS INTEGER)` or REAL conversion
282	may order or allocate commits. The association only copies a counter already
283	allocated by the guarded receipt writer. F37 exercises the 2/9/10/100 ordering
284	and uint64-maximum conversion counterexamples; source review checks that every
285	ordering call uses the one accessor.
286	
287	The host's live session supplies the independent `executionId` ↔ `operationRef`
288	association. The latter retains security's `op-` plus 32 lowercase hex grammar;
289	it is not an ExecutionId with a different prefix. Validate the exact namespace,
290	store binding, Run, inventory, receipt bytes, security carrier, grant generation,
291	SEAL sequence/body hash and operation binding. Verify receipt schema and
292	signer/custody, the journal's owner hash chain and the retained replayable objects.
293	Matching just RunId, a digest or a current database row does not establish those
294	joins. Metadata canonicalization and product-data canonicalization stay separate.
295	
296	### Witness-aware publication and read-only recovery
297	
298	The inherited security v8 §5.4 witness protocol is part of the carrier boundary.
299	Final SEAL publication must complete its **PENDING witness → journal transaction
300	commit/barrier → COMMITTED witness** sequence before the evidence-ledger commit.
301	The broad journal record schema's i64 `seq` allowance does not override the
302	carrier's uint53 cap or reserved terminal slot: ordinary SEAL uses at most
303	`9007199254740990`; slot `9007199254740991` remains TERMINAL. Capacity handling
304	must finish through lifecycle outside the held operation lease, never by taking
305	its fence backwards inside commit.
306	
307	The inherited `security-schemas.v2/grant-journal.sql` does not admit SEAL in its
308	record-type CHECK and still names historical platform aliases. It is historical
309	carrier evidence, not ready-to-use product DDL. **COV-03** requires an explicitly
310	versioned product carrier migration that admits current schema-3 SEAL/current
311	platform records while preserving historical row interpretation, append-only
312	hash chains, reserved capacity, witness/high-water checks and the S9 reader/core
313	bridge. Do not disable SQL checks or relabel old rows as current. A journal's own
314	SQLite transaction is distinct from the evidence ledger transaction; holding
315	the prescribed lock order does not make the two databases atomically committed.
316	The proposal orders both level-3 write transactions before the level-4 append
317	lock: grant journal, then evidence ledger. Every journal writer, including the
318	revocation observer, must use the same security-owned transaction-before-append
319	API; no caller may acquire a new journal transaction from inside an append-lock
320	callback. A failed second acquisition rolls back/releases the first. Committing
321	the journal releases its DB transaction while the append lock stays held through
322	the witness and evidence commit; no journal transaction is reacquired there.
323	Claude must review this refinement against S7 and every inherited journal writer.
324	
325	Read-only recovery may inspect a consistent ledger snapshot and the admitted
326	carrier/witness/floor state. It must not perform witness INIT, REVERT or ADVANCE,
327	raise trust high-water, allocate a store binding or obtain a new execution grant.
328	If reconciliation of the requested attempt's carrier prefix is needed, report
329	the owner diagnosis and inability to confirm current local custody; an
330	authorized lifecycle open performs the lawful mutation,
331	then a new read-only recovery can retry. A mere absent or malformed witness never
332	licenses repair. The ordinary writer lifecycle's existing start/end high-water
333	handoff stays separate from a read-only request.
334	
335	A journal tail ahead of the witness, a missing witness for nonempty history,
336	a lower-than-observed tail, an equal sequence with different hash, unknown schema
337	or contradictory receipt/association is a custody/recovery refusal. A verified
338	empty exact ledger lookup can establish that an attempt did not commit; an
339	unreadable ledger, another generation, the requested attempt still running or
340	an unresolved witness for its required prefix cannot. Active-attempt recovery
341	may report in-progress/undetermined and must not declare a final failure from an
342	older read snapshot. A valid later append's PENDING witness does not invalidate
343	an earlier committed receipt: snapshot readers verify its retained durable
344	prefix and never wait for the writer or repair the newer witness. Ordinary
345	historical queries do not reuse current execution grants or turn each read into
346	whole-carrier recovery.
347	
348	Preserve the recovery association, exact receipt, store-generation lineage and
349	required journal verification material while their local commitment is retained.
350	They are operational custody state under G19, not disposable indexes. Removing
351	or compacting a journal generation requires an explicitly reviewed retained
352	verification bridge; absence of that bridge prevents deletion. This proposal
353	does not alter immutable assurance or claim that purge deletes exported copies.
354	
355	Before the atomic commit-admission gate, recheck the observer latch and
356	freshness/cancellation after any blocking journal/witness or association-staging
357	operation. SEAL may already be durable; a failed final checkpoint
358	latches fail-stop and rolls back the still-uncommitted evidence transaction.
359	Release the append lock and remaining carrier transaction resources before a
360	fresh lawful journal append records REV/cleanup under the stopped operation
361	lease, then release that lease and perform the S7 end handoff; never
362	reacquire a level-3 journal transaction under level 4. No further effect is
363	admitted from the failed session. The old SEAL remains an uncommitted attempt. The journal lock
364	orders REV against commit; it cannot bound an OS syscall stalled indefinitely.
365	S6 scheduling assumptions and real platform measurements remain required.
366

374	| `executionId` | `execution` | Exact host attempt ExecutionId and receipt executionId; never derived from operationRef. |
375	| `runId` | `run` | Byte-equal evaluator RunId, SEAL runId and receipt runId; current run3 only. |
376	| `inventoryDigest` | `hex64` | Exact admitted retention inventory and receipt inventoryDigest. |

378	| `receiptBytesSha256` | `hex64` | Raw SHA-256 of the exact stored receipt bytes; verify its selected schema and signer/custody separately. |
379	| `journalCarrierDigest` | `hex64` | Existing journal projectKeyDigest from the security-owned carrier binding, not a hash of a caller-supplied path. |

386	
387	Conclusions below are internal scenario expectations, not new public D9

On failure latch fail-stop, abort evidence transaction, release ordered locks, then record REV through a new lawful journal call; never reacquire level3 under level4. Actual syscall stall bounds require qualification. |

Recovery metadata needs a retention root; lawful migrations preserve its verification lineage. |

A later valid PENDING journal append does not block confirmation of an earlier durable prefix. A snapshot missing an actively running requested attempt is not final absence. |

1492	## 5. Durable custody and failure protocol
1493	
1494	Default `opensip`/`analyze` is DURABLE_AUTHORITATIVE under CD-RT-5. The host
1495	reports retention origin DEFAULTED and durable-unbounded posture before first
1496	write; the command's documented effect is admission of the project marker and
1497	private registry/store, followed by an authoritative Run. No implicit policy
1498	file is written. Explicit retention overrides have independent byte/time/count
1499	bounds with provenance; failure to satisfy an authoritative request never
1500	silently demotes it to ephemeral. `--ephemeral` is explicitly non-authoritative,
1501	uses temporary custody, mints no authoritative commit receipt and cannot satisfy
1502	baseline adoption, repair or authoritative replay prerequisites.
1503	
1504	The storage-root admission still applies the inherited sync, backup and private
1505	custody classifications separately. A detected backup-managed root requires an
1506	explicit storage-policy choice before the first source-derived write (TM V17):
1507	select another admitted root, choose explicit ephemeral mode, or acknowledge
1508	backup custody for this invocation with `--allow-backup-custody` (or the
1509	corresponding already-admitted host storage-policy record). CI never prompts;
1510	without that explicit choice it refuses REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED with detail
1511	`storage.backup-choice-required`, before creating evidence. The acknowledgement
1512	is retained as operational custody metadata; it does not alter semantic Run
1513	identity or silently write a policy file. UNKNOWN backup status is disclosed as
1514	unknown, never as not-backed-up. Purge never claims deletion of external copies.
1515	Sync/upload roots and group/ACL exposure retain their separate admission rules;
1516	a backup acknowledgement is not a network-export or shared-storage grant.
1517	
1518	Exactly one per-project writer holds the lifecycle lease/fence through source
1519	admission, evaluation and atomic commit. Read-only clients use a consistent
1520	committed ledger snapshot and never wait while holding a lock needed by the
1521	writer. Global trust admission and revocation use the security contract's lock
1522	order. SQLite WAL, transaction settings, fsync/atomic-rename carrier and crash
1523	reconciliation retain the reviewed lifecycle carrier's native obligations;
1524	the reference model here tests the semantic transition, not OS durability.
1525	
1526	Commit order:
1527	
1528	1. Validate closure and independently replay proof; compute all final IDs.
1529	2. Write immutable blobs and descriptors to private temporary files, verify
1530	   digest/length, fsync files, atomically publish under digest, fsync directories.
1531	3. In one synchronous ledger transaction insert Run manifest, object references,
1532	   retained availability generation, baseline/other authorized pins and a commit
1533	   receipt with ExecutionId, namespace, monotonic sequence, inventory digest,
1534	   signer and immutable assurance; commit and satisfy the carrier's barriers.
1535	4. Only then acknowledge commitment. Required rendering/delivery is later and
1536	   cannot rewrite the Run. Receipt signing is operational custody evidence and
1537	   excluded from semantic IDs; the receipt authenticates RunId and inventory.
1538	
1539	A failure before step 3 publishes no authoritative Run. Orphan blobs are
1540	unreferenced and eligible for GC after reconciliation. A crash after ledger
1541	commit but before acknowledgement is `durability-undetermined` to the caller,
1542	exit 4, with an ExecutionId for read-only recovery. Recovery checks the ledger
1543	and actual objects; it returns committed or failed, never repeats a repository
1544	mutation. Duplicate retry can share a Run but has a separate attempt receipt.
1545	An acknowledged Run with missing/corrupt objects becomes partially available or
1546	corrupt; the host does not pretend it was never sealed.
1547	
1548	Sealed assurance is immutable: verified means exact identity+proof checks at
1549	seal; verifiable also commits the verification closure; replayable also commits
1550	all exact admitted producer executables and source/input closure. The default
1551	authoritative profile requires replayable retention at seal. Current
1552	availability is a separate monotonic-generation record: retained, partial,
1553	expired, purged, corrupt or unavailable, with exact missing references and
1554	cause. Availability may improve through verified restoration or regeneration;
1555	sealed assurance and historical verdict never change. A query reports both.
1556	
1557	Retention roots include every live Run's required closure, active baseline,
1558	authorized repair prerequisite and backup/export operation pin. Automatic
1559	expiry respects these pins and all independent policy bounds; it refuses a
1560	new durable admission if the required closure cannot be retained within bounds.
1561	A direct purge of a pinned Run refuses unless the explicit destructive purge
1562	also revokes the named pins after disclosing consequences. That refusal has a
1563	registered public projection and this contract does not restate it: the
1564	foundation-owned detail `evidence.pinned` projects as `request-rejected`,
1565	`REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED`, exit 2, carrying the closed
1566	`common.schema.json#/$defs/PinnedPurgeDisclosure` — the RunId, the complete
1567	current `activePins` inventory sorted uniquely by `pinId`, and the three ordered
1568	consequences `named-pins-revoked`,
1569	`dependent-evidence-replay-unavailable`, `sealed-history-retained` — exactly as
1570	**workflows-and-surfaces §12** specifies. No pin is omitted, truncated or
1571	aggregated into a count. Neither that disclosure nor any flag confers authority:
1572	a later destructive attempt still requires the explicit lifecycle authorization
1573	and disclosure of its then-current complete pin set, and a changed pin inventory
1574	requires renewed disclosure before destruction. Purge retains the
1575	minimal sealed manifest, provenance and tombstone but deletes unshared evidence
1576	bytes by reachability GC; shared bytes survive until the final reference is
1577	removed. Purged is not deleted-history. The user may separately destroy the
1578	whole project store/marker under lifecycle authorization; no indefinite privacy
1579	claim is made for backups or exports already outside that store.
1580	
1581	A retention decision never changes a fact, Coverage, finding or Run identity.
1582	It never turns expired evidence into `no match`. Query of retained manifest is
1583	allowed after purge and states evidence unavailable. Query requiring actual
1584	proof, comparison baseline or repair input refuses with
1585	REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED and `evidence.{expired,purged,missing,corrupt}`
1586	before evaluation (exit 2); inability during a selected operation is HOST.IO_FAILURE
1587	with evidence detail (exit 4). Successfully admitted partial native inputs may
1588	instead produce an indeterminate Run (exit 3) under the native and D9 contracts.
1589	These are different event positions, not interchangeable error spellings.
1590	
1591	Backup/export holds a read snapshot plus short-lived object pins, writes a
1592	bounded relative-path inventory, hashes and verifies every object, then seals
1593	the bundle. Import checks path traversal, symlinks, sizes, duplicate paths,
1594	cryptographic identities and all referenced schemas before publishing anything.
